chunks: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, completes the obligatory salat (prayer) with the supererogatory prayer, completes the obligatory fasting with the supererogatory fasting, and completes the wudu (ablution) with the ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday.

key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory or recommended act of worship
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةَ: salat (prayer), here referring first to the obligatory prayer and then to the supererogatory prayer

ai.seo_question: How are obligatory acts of worship completed by recommended acts in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, perfects obligatory acts of worship through recommended devotional acts. It highlights the role of supererogatory salat (prayer), fasting, and the Friday ghusl (ritual bath) in completing and enhancing a believer’s worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.231 – (Al-Hussain ibn Khalid asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Awwal (as)) narrates that:

‘It is narrated that 'Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, completes the obligatory prayer with the supererogatory prayer, completes the obligatory fasting with the supererogatory fasting, and completes the wudu (ablution) with the ghusl (ritual bath) of Jumu’ah.’.
